correctness.rationale: For all integer t>=1 and real r>=1, the proof directly establishes fPO by crossed fractional exchanges and global positive-weighted-sum optimality. The EFX constraint reduces to a single exact bound on a labeled subset size. Symmetric family inclusion-exclusion, r=1 exact balance, precise jump equalities, and Stirling tail bounds prove all claimed cases. A standard-library independently coded exact verifier checked 356,980 allocations across 85 rational instances and every applicable small jump equality; this is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

evidence: Aziz et al. (2022), arXiv:2211.00879, Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 5.1, concern fPO and EFX respectively, not the simultaneous all-optima count.
Garg, Murhekar and Qin (2022), arXiv:2212.02440, prove EFX+fPO existence for specified bivalued instances, a strictly weaker statement than the exact census.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Any broad theorem enumerating EFX+fPO allocations for arbitrary two-agent positive bivalued disutilities would subsume this one, but no such theorem was found in the inspected primary sources or record searches. Existence does not determine counts, threshold jumps, or entropy, while broad fPO structure needs a new EFX counting argument.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The published fPO characterization implies only the admissible efficiency families. Its conjunction with EFX existence does not quantify their intersection or its weighted labeling multiplicities. The counting result follows after imposing a separate sharp EFX inequality, counting labeled subsets, and evaluating binomial-tail asymptotics. The earlier theorems cover a crucial proof ingredient, but no covering joint-count result was located.

Their full 29-page source and Garg et al. arXiv:2212.02440 were inspected for any dominating joint-count or entropy statement; none was found. Actual mathematical-record queries and local ledger-claim comparisons disclosed no covering equivalent. Priority is not certain for unindexed work or overlooked corollaries.

value.rationale: The exact count of all jointly EFX and fPO allocations, rational phase thresholds and a discontinuous change in uniform-allocation probability quantify the size and robustness of the feasible fair-and-efficient set in a natural symmetric two-type chore model. This answers a structural classification/counting question beyond mere existence; it gives precise integer cutoffs and sharp asymptotic rates relevant to randomized allocation methods.
